description: Random init baseline; prints the task object's public attributes and the token ids the model receives.
Place-value attention parser, 1000 tied 3-unit ReLU steps of (a,b)->(|a-b|,min(a,b)), attention readout with parabolic head.
Same circuit as EuclidTied1000; Euclid block graded on all 10^6 pairs, parser and readout on every g, to measure the exact tied-step count.
Tied (a,b)->(b,D(a,b)) where D is a 16-knot one-layer ReLU triangular wave (distance to nearest multiple of b); readout takes A+B.
Fold Euclid with 16 knots at its exact all-pairs step budget of 250 (FoldK16N200 reached only 99.92% of pairs despite 200/200 on eval).
Fold Euclid with 64 knots and 70 tied steps, testing the prediction that steps fall as roughly 4000/K.
Fold Euclid with 2000 knots so the wave covers A's full range with no tail; measures the true least-absolute-remainder Euclid depth.
Narrow end of the width-depth curve: fold Euclid with 4 knots, step budget 1000.
Tied round of three composed folds at scales 25b, 5b, b with 10 knots each, so reach multiplies instead of adding.
Three-scale fold cascade at its exact all-pairs budget of 14 rounds (42 MLP layers, 32 hidden units in total).
Binary long division in weights: ten 2-knot folds at scales 512b down to b, one quotient bit per layer, tied over 10 rounds.
Binary long division fold cascade at its exact all-pairs budget of 9 rounds (22 hidden units, 90 MLP layers after tying).
Binary long division with unused weights removed: attention addresses by position and carries 4 state channels, folds touch only (A,B), head reads only X.
Slim binary long division in float32 to test whether inexact attention-parsed integers break the exact-zero Euclid fixed point.
Six single-digit attention heads with place values in W_o, so A and B are exact integers; float32 again to confirm this fixes the noise failure.
DigitHeadsFloat32 graded end to end through the full model on all 10^6 prompts, closing the gap left by the composed check.
Removes the 512b fold (nine folds, 256b down to b) with a 12-round budget to see whether it is needed.
Only six folds (32b down to b) with a 40-round budget, to measure how rounds grow as reach per round shrinks.
Eight folds (128b down to b) with a 14-round budget, looking for the fold count that minimises total layers.
Seven folds (64b down to b) with a 14-round budget, the last binary chain between the 9-round and 32-round regimes.
Best binary chain at its minimum: eight folds (128b down to b), 9 rounds, 72 fold layers; also reports the nonzero weight count.
Attention keys store only addressed positions (+BIG) and leave ignored positions at 0, removing the -BIG filler weights.
Schoolbook decimal long division: three 10-knot folds at scales 100b, 10b, b, trading knots for fewer layers per round.
Decimal long division at its exact all-pairs budget of 9 rounds: 27 fold layers and 32 hidden units.
Radix-4 division: four 4-knot folds at scales 64b, 16b, 4b, b (18 hidden units), testing whether Euclid depth stays at 9 rounds.
Radix-4 division with an added 256b fold (five 4-knot folds, 22 hidden units), testing whether 9 rounds suffice.
Radix-8 division: three 8-knot folds at scales 64b, 8b, b (26 hidden units), the remaining point on the depth versus sparsity curve.
Negative control: one round fewer than the measured minimum of 9, which should produce wrong answers if that minimum is real.
Control on Radix8N9: head centers at d+0.5 instead of d+0.495, putting exact integers on the decision boundary.
Control on Radix8N9: head centers at d+0.45, moving the boundary below the safe window so fractions of 0.95 and up should misfloor.
Radix8N9 with attention gain BIG lowered from 40 to 10, testing how much softmax leakage the exact-integer Euclid can tolerate.
Radix8N9 with BIG=25, just above the roughly 24 predicted from softmax leakage against float32 precision.
Radix8N9 with BIG=20, just below the roughly 24 predicted from softmax leakage against float32 precision, expected to fail.
No swap: A is folded by B, then B by A, each with radix-8 folds. Gives a true fixed point and no carry units, with a 6-round budget.
No-swap design with sparser radix-4 folds (64b down to b for each register), 8-round budget, testing whether it closes the weight gap to swap.
Control on NoSwapRadix4N8: folds run fine to coarse (b up to 64b) instead of coarse to fine, testing whether long-division order matters.
Radix8N9 with one attention query shared by all heads in each layer, removing the duplicated query weights.
Radix4N12 with shared attention queries: the sparsest candidate, 18 hidden units over 48 fold layers.
Control on SharedQueryRadix4N12: 3 knots per fold instead of 4, so the wave ends on slope -1 and D(g,0) should no longer equal g.
Final model: SharedQueryRadix4N12 with positions as a fixed one-hot buffer. Euclid by radix-4 folds, 12 tied rounds, 0/10^6 wrong end to end in float32.
